summary: John Claude White (1853–1918) was a scholar in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He studied at Rugby School in 1868 and at the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873–1876), becoming an Assistant Engineer in the Bengal Public Works Department in 1876.

John Clifford Holt (b. 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Gustavus Adolphus College, Graduate Theological Union, and the University of Chicago under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah, he taught primarily at Bowdoin College (1978–2019) alongside visiting posts at Chicago and Berkeley.

John Cockburn Thomson (1834–1860) was an Indology scholar who earned his B.A. from Trinity College, Oxford (1852–1857). During his education, he studied under Christian Lassen (~1851–1855) and Horace Hayman Wilson (1852–1857).

John Collinson Nesfield (1836–1919) was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Highgate School and Merton College, Oxford (~1856–1862). He held professorships at Presidency University and Krishnagar Government College, later serving as principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University in 1878.
John Correia-Afonso (1924–2005) worked in the field of history and archaeology. He studied under Henry Heras from approximately 1949 to 1953 and later succeeded him.

John Corrigan (b. 1952) is a religious studies scholar who earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1978–1982). His career includes positions at Harvard, the University of Virginia, Arizona State University, and Florida State University, where he chaired the religion department.

John Crawfurd (1783–1868) was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. He earned an M.D. from the University of Edinburgh (~1800–1803), served as a physician for the East India Company (1803–1808), and succeeded Stamford Raffles in 1823.
John Cripps Pembrey (1832–1916) worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as the Oriental Reader at Clarendon Press, with his appointment attested in 1904 and 1916.

John Cumming (1868–1958) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his education at the University of Glasgow (~1884–1888) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1888–1890), and served as Vice-Chairman at SOAS University of London from 1925 to 1946.

John D'Oyly (1774–1824) was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He completed his education at the University of Cambridge, earning a B.A. from Corpus Christi College between approximately 1792 and 1796.

John D. Dunne (b. 1961) specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied at Amherst, Harvard, and CIHTS, and held academic appointments at Emory University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison, where he became Distinguished Professor of Contemplative Humanities in 2015.

John D. Kelly is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. He has served at the University of Chicago, where he was attested as Christian W. Mackauer Professor of Anthropology and of Social Sciences.

John D. Smith (b. 1946) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London (1975) and was later University Lecturer in Sanskrit (1984) and Professor (2001–2007) at the University of Cambridge.

John Daido Loori (1931–2009) was a Buddhist studies practitioner and scholar who studied at Rutgers University and under Soen Nakagawa and Taizan Maezumi. He taught at Naropa University in 1974 and served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery from ~1980 to 2009.
John Daishin Buksbazen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at the Zen Center of Los Angeles and trained under Taizan Maezumi and Bernie Glassman.

John David Paterson (1754–1809) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He joined the East India Company in 1776, co-founded The Asiatic Society, and served as a Judge and Magistrate at the University of Dhaka.

John David Rees (1854–1922) was an Indologist educated at Cheltenham College. He served in the Madras Civil Service (1875), the Indian Civil Service (~1875–1901), and on the Council of India as an Additional Member (1895–1900).

John Dawson Mayne (1828–1917) was an Indologist educated at Trinity College Dublin (~1845–1849). He served as Professor of Law at Presidency College, Chennai (~1857–1872) and later as Professor of Common Law at the Inns of Court (1880–1885).

John DeFrancis (1911–2009) was a sinologist and linguist who studied at Columbia University (~1937–1941) and Yale University (~1945–1947). He held academic posts at Seton Hall University (~1961–1966) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1966–1976).

John Dewey (1859–1952) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Vermont (~1875–1879) and Johns Hopkins University (~1882–1884). He held professorships at the universities of Michigan, Minnesota, Chicago (~1894–1904), and Columbia University (~1904–1930).
